subtitle: Level-Dependent Drive
tagline: Six drive curves, a level-dependent response, an independent TB character layer, and a steep focus range, from polished heat to unstable, broken textures.

body.lead: TB Distortion adds harmonics and grit with two independent layers: a main drive stage with six nonlinear curves, and a TB character layer that adds Level, Sample, Time, or Bias texture alongside it.

body.p: A steep focus range limits the distortion to the band you choose, so you can dirty up the midrange of a bass while its low end stays clean. The parallel blend and output trim let you mix the result back in at a matched level.

ul: Six drive curves: Soft, Hard, Fuzz, Tube, Tape, and Fold
Dynamics: make the drive respond to level, pushing peaks harder or preserving transients
Independent TB character layer with four types and its own amount
Focus range with 48 dB/oct low and high limits
DC blocking at 10 Hz and 4x oversampling
Eight factory distortion concepts plus user presets

note.title: About this manual
text: This manual describes TB Distortion 1.3.0 for Windows (VST3). The current macOS build is version 1.0.3 and may differ from the descriptions here.

ol: Insert TB Distortion on a track. It starts with the Soft curve, `DRIVE` 6 dB, and `MIX` 100%.
Choose a curve in `TYPE` {{4}} and raise `DRIVE` {{5}} until you hear the amount of grit you want.
Move `DYNAMICS` {{6}}: positive values drive peaks harder; negative values keep transients clean.
Set `LOW` and `HIGH` {{9}} to distort only the part of the spectrum that needs it.
Add texture with `TB TYPE` {{7}} and `TB DRIVE` {{8}} if you want an extra, unstable character.
Lower `MIX` {{10}} for parallel distortion and match the level with `OUTPUT`.

Base drive into the selected curve. Higher values add more harmonics and compression.
Level-dependent drive. Positive values drive peaks harder; negative values preserve transients. It shapes the drive's response and is not a compressor.
Gentle, rounded saturation. A good starting point for warmth.

Wavefolding: the waveform folds back on itself, creating bright, metallic overtones.

body.p: The TB layer is a separate stage that works on the raw input, next to the main drive. Its amount does not depend on the drive type or the DRIVE setting, so you can change the curve without losing a TB texture you like.

rows: Independent Level, Sample, Time, or Bias jitter on the raw-input layer.
Independent TB distortion amount, unaffected by the drive type or amount. High values add more harmonics.

body.p: Choose a preset from the PRESET list {{1}} or step through them with the arrows {{3}}. SAVE stores the current settings as a .tbpreset file, and LOAD opens one.

Factory concepts: **Clean Heat**, **Tube Bloom**, **Diode Crack**, **Broken Cone**, **Worn Reel**, **Parallel Mid Dirt**, **Folded Motion**, and **Radio Breakdown**. **Init** resets to the default settings.
Starting points for common jobs. Adjust them by ear and compare at matched loudness.

recipes.title: Warm up a vocal or bus
recipes.use: Subtle density and harmonics without obvious distortion.
steps: Raise DRIVE until the sound thickens, then lower MIX until it is just noticeable.

recipes.title: Dirty bass that keeps its low end
recipes.use: Growl in the midrange with a clean, solid bottom.
steps: Set LOW above the fundamental so the low end stays undistorted.
Blend with MIX and match OUTPUT.

recipes.title: Lo-fi radio voice
steps: Try each TB TYPE to change how unstable the voice sounds.

recipes.title: Keep drums punchy
recipes.use: Saturate drums without losing the attack.
steps: Lower DYNAMICS until the transients come through clearly again.
